body:
[A10] **Round 6 for [A605], and a precision to the corrected ruling.** R629-5 is POSITIVE ([6134076275](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/729#issuecomment-6134076275)). R628-5 is NEGATIVE ([6134115312](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/729#issuecomment-6134115312)) on one MINOR finding. The refresh allowance is measured in the same run, so any lateness counts as "service" and widens its own bound. Schedulers planted at 1600 ms and 2000 ms, and a 900 ms egress stall, all pass.

**Precision to 6132483068.** The service delay in the refresh condition is a fixed ceiling stated once in the contract, not a figure taken from the run under test. It is **25 ms**: the largest measured service was about 12 ms (1012.029 ms gaps at the largest shape), plus margin. The refresh condition is therefore: every gap between consecutive notifications for one changed descriptor and one recipient is at most **1025 ms**. The spacing condition (at least the rate limit) is unchanged.

1. **R628-5-F1.** Grade every gap against the fixed 1025 ms bound at both shapes. Record the measured service per descriptor for information only. R628-5's `probe_counters.py` plants (`sched-1600`, `sched-2000`, `egress-stall`), unchanged, must each FAIL by name. The correct RTL passes, and the start-shift invariance arm keeps its outcome.
2. **Texts.** `docs/testing/726_STREAM_COUNTERS.md:61-62`, the PR body and any other text that states the bound name the fixed 25 ms ceiling and its source.
3. **Residue.** Apply R628-5's residue and R629-5's body residue. R628-5's suggestion is optional.

Post REVIEW READY with the head.
